body.x: Ahead of the opening of FIX 2026 (Future Innovation Tech Expo), a four-day event beginning Wednesday, October 21, Daegu Metropolitan City announced that 31 companies boasting innovative technologies and products have been selected as recipients of the ‘FIX 2026 Innovation Awards’.

The Innovation Awards recognize enterprises possessing world-class innovative technologies across mobility, AI/ICT, and robotics. A panel of 26 domestic and international expert evaluators selected 9 companies for the Best Innovation Technology Award and 22 companies for the Innovation Award. A total of 209 companies applied this year, with over 70%—147 companies—holding prior award-winning track records at prominent domestic and international exhibitions, including CES. Among the 31 recipients, 6 are regional companies based in Daegu.

By sector, future mobility accounted for 6 companies (4 Best Innovation Technology Awards, 2 Innovation Awards), robotics accounted for 8 companies (2 Best Innovation Technology Awards, 6 Innovation Awards), and AI/ICT accounted for 17 companies (3 Best Innovation Technology Awards, 14 Innovation Awards).

In future mobility, SWM received the Best Innovation Technology Award for its ‘Physical AI-based Urban Robotaxi’, a zone-based door-to-door transit service operating in Gangnam, Seoul, without fixed routes, dynamically responding to passenger pickup requests and destinations. Having launched South Korea’s first late-night autonomous driving service in September 2024, SWM recently initiated paid commercial operations. It is solidifying its foundation for Level 4 fully driverless commercialization by integrating its next-generation 2,000 TOPS autonomous driving computing platform, ‘AP-700’, which processes advanced AI models and massive sensor streams in real time. Within the same category, ONEPREDICT’s ‘AI-Native Solution’, PERSEUS’s software-defined vehicle (SDV) hypervisor solution ‘Pegasus’, and HJWAVE’s ‘3D Waveguide Antenna’ were also honored with Best Innovation Technology Awards.

body.x: In the robotics sector, Best Innovation Technology Awards went to AeiROBOT for ‘Alice 5’ and Tesollo for its ‘DG-5F-M Humanoid Multi-Joint Robot Hand’. Standing 170 cm tall and weighing 50 kg, Alice 5 is a bipedal humanoid robot featuring a proprietary hybrid actuation architecture that combines quasi-direct drive (QDD) actuators in the upper body with linear actuators in the lower limbs. It can walk stably while carrying heavy, asymmetrical equipment. Unlike single-purpose robots, it can swap modular end-effector hands to execute diverse tasks, ranging from repetitive industrial operations to precision assembly. This technology is expected to address labor shortages driven by aging demographics while elevating industrial safety standards.

body.x: In AI/ICT, CENS secured the Best Innovation Technology Award for its ‘AI-Controlled Precision Spray Cooling System’. The solution employs forced-convection cooling that disrupts thermal boundary layers by spraying a non-conductive dielectric fluid directly onto high-heat AI server components, achieving ultra-high cooling efficiency by dynamically optimizing pump flow rates through AI-driven real-time TDP-tracking algorithms and VFD controls. While conventional tank-based liquid immersion risks spreading faults across an entire server tank upon a single localized failure, spray cooling eliminates this vulnerability through an automated isolation architecture for anomalous racks, marking a world-first commercialization. POTATONET’s AI-based deep web threat intelligence solution ‘Owl’ and WACE’s ‘VEXPLOR Manufacturing AI Software’ were also named recipients of the Best Innovation Technology Award.

Among regional recipients of the Innovation Award, standout companies included Remplir, UND Robotics, and Farmity. Remplir’s ‘Industrial Next-Gen EV Mobility Customized Domestic LFP Prismatic Battery and Module Pack’ offers an optimized energy storage solution for industrial electric vehicles and purpose-built future mobility, applicable to electric forklifts, AGVs/AMRs, agricultural machinery, construction equipment, and golf carts. UND Robotics’ ‘Magbot Automatic Tool Changer’ is an automatic tool changer (ATC) system that swaps diverse end-effectors to perform multi-process operations, powered solely by a 24V supply and requiring no pneumatic lines or air compressors. It integrates seamlessly with standard industrial arms, battery-powered AMRs and AGVs, and humanoid platforms.

Farmity’s ‘FIVIS_SafeX’ is a Spatial AI-driven industrial safety platform that leverages existing CCTV feeds and mobile cameras mounted on forklifts and industrial vehicles to recognize and analyze worksite hazards. By comprehensively tracking workers, vehicles, machinery, and restricted zones, it detects falls, collision risks, fire outbreaks, unauthorized intrusions, and personal protective equipment (PPE) compliance in real time. Because it upgrades safety infrastructure without requiring camera replacements, it is readily deployable across manufacturing, logistics, and construction sites. Farmity previously made history as the first Daegu-based company to win two CES 2026 Innovation Awards across the AI and Digital Health categories.

body.x: Additional Innovation Award recipients included Quantum HiTech for ‘TRIZ-AI™’, an AI platform for non-destructive cell-level battery diagnostics using real-world EV driving data; Unmanned Exploration Laboratory for the ‘SCARAB Selfie-Cam Rotating Axis Rover, Avant-Garde Blazer’; Beyond Robotics for ‘PICKY’, a Physical AI-based autonomous fruit and vegetable harvesting robot; Zio Robot for its smart modular mobile robot for multi-robot collaboration; 3DT Solution for ‘ZEROS’, an AI autonomous ultra-close precision firefighting robot; GEOBOT for its Physical AI-based autonomous sinkhole exploration robot; Crosshub for ‘V-Pay’, a voice biometric payment security solution; Arame Materials for its eco-friendly, high-barrier moisture and oxygen protective coating derived from seaweed cellulose; Braincheese for the ‘BRC AX cube’ on-device AI safety monitoring system; VISIONSPACE for ‘TESSERACT’, an integrated web platform delivering end-to-end AI training workflows within web browsers; AES Tech for ‘ammoNOVA Ultra’, an AI-driven liquefied ammonia hydrogen extraction system; MedySapiens for ‘MedyCVI’, an AI-based software medical device for genetic disease diagnosis; Digitalog Technologies for ‘Conma AI’, a social media channel transformation and automated operations platform; StealCut for ‘StealCut Protect’, a facial image protection solution that fundamentally thwarts deepfakes; CNS for ‘DIMS’, a drone infrastructure management platform for automated tower crane inspections; Quantum Aero for ‘Quantonomy Copilot’, a natural-language mission OS for drones; WES-Tec Global for ‘Revocle’, an AI-powered closed-loop plastic recycling manufacturing system; Ginnolab for zero-power radiative cooling nano-ceramic coatings for AI data centers; and WISEAI for its ‘AiU’ AI medical care platform.

The presentation ceremony for the Best Innovation Technology Awards (top 9 enterprises) and Innovation Awards (the remaining 22 enterprises representing the top 15%) is scheduled for Thursday, October 22, at the EXCO East Wing Open Seminar Room during FIX 2026. Official honors will comprise two Ministerial Commendations from the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, two Ministerial Commendations from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, three Daegu Mayoral Commendations, and two Chairman’s Awards from the Korea Credit Guarantee Fund.

Daegu Mayor Kyungho Choo stated, “The FIX Innovation Awards serve as a springboard for companies possessing outstanding innovative technologies to gain international recognition and grow into global market leaders. We look forward to the continued interest and proactive participation of visionary enterprises worldwide that are shaping the future of technology.”

Marking its third edition, FIX 2026 (Future Innovation Tech Expo) is a future-industry exhibition that converges and connects cutting-edge technologies across future mobility, robotics, AI/ICT, and startups, running from Wednesday, October 21 to Saturday, October 24 at EXCO in Daegu. Under the theme “AI, Beyond Tech into Reality,” the event facilitates the sharing of industrial trends and pivotal technologies through AI-driven exhibits, international conferences and lectures by leading experts, and specialized global networking programs.
